title: What The Trumpet Knows (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 106bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal music philosophy absurdist brass
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The trumpet is the loudest thing in the orchestra by a distance
And everyone in the orchestra maintains a safe clearance
The trumpet player knows this and sits at the back right corner
Which is where the loudest person always is — a fair warning

[Pre-Chorus]
I once sat in front of a trumpet at a school concert in December
I heard it clearly from two and a half metres — I still remember

[Chorus]
What does the trumpet know that I don't know?
It knows that projection is the thing that runs the show
What does the trumpet know at nine in the morning?
It knows the whole house is awake without any warning
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
The jazz trumpet is a different animal from the classical
It bends the notes with the valve and the lip — it's not categorical
The same instrument in Dizzy and in a parade on Tuesday
Sounds like two completely different relationships with the today

[Bridge]
There was a trumpet player once in the jazzclub in Fremantle
Who played an A at concert pitch and it went through the mantle
Of the building and came out on the other side fully intact
The trumpet had made its position clear and that was that

[Outro]
Trumpet knows… projection is the argument… trumpet knows
That's my boy
